explanation: Dufour cites Bolton as authority that the prosecutor's remark was permissible comment on evidence, not on silence; Kinchen (1985) had disapproved Bolton's test for such comments (from my knowledge; no excerpt). No mention of Kinchen; separate litigation.

citing_name: State ex rel. Clark v. Long
explanation: Court cites Buckles for the rule that the Interstate Agreement on Detainers applies only if a detainer is lodged; Waller abrogated Buckles on a different point, victim's prior violent acts in self-defense (my knowledge), so limb 1 fails.

citing_name: Commonwealth ex rel. City of Allentown v. Howells
cited_name: Louts K. Liggett Co. v. Baldridge
explanation: Liggett is cited only for a corporation being a 'person' under due process; Snyder's Drug overruled its substantive due process holding on pharmacy ownership laws (my knowledge), a different point, so limb 1 fails.

citing_court: Supreme Court of the Territory of Hawaii
explanation: McCargo is the movant's authority, which the court declines to follow, denying the motion; the disapproval reached only the mandamus suggestion, not finality, and the opinion expressly notes that disapproval.

Nevada court cites Fiscus (See) to support its rationale that the contractee bears insurance cost and so shares immunity; Piper had overruled Fiscus in its entirety 19 days earlier. No acknowledgment; unrelated litigation.

Colorado court quotes Felch as authority for excluding a deceased's declarations of intention as hearsay; Trefethen (1892) overruled Felch on exactly that point. No mention of Trefethen in the passage; unrelated litigation.

Loomis is cited for the rule that moral obligation is not consideration; Rand v. Mather overruled only its statute of frauds holding that a partly void contract is wholly void (my knowledge), so limb 1 fails.

citing_name: Slater v. Director, Division of Taxation
explanation: Tax Court cites Seltzer only for the summary-judgment standard (doubts resolved against movant). Lyon v. Barrett overruled Seltzer's substantive legal-malpractice holding (own knowledge; no excerpt), a different point, so limb 1 fails.

Lee cites Fisher and Holmes as support that a larceny verdict must declare value and reverses on it; Griffith (1913) had overruled both outright on that verdict-value rule (own knowledge; no excerpt). No mention of Griffith.

Alaska court adopts the per se reversal rule for jury separation, citing D'Antonio and 'See' Panczko as authority; Arciniega had overruled both on that rule 18 days earlier. No negative history noted; unrelated litigation.

citing_court: Court of Appeal of the State of California
explanation: Oliver relies on Haehlen for the nuisance rule that courts cannot set aesthetic standards absent legislation; Varney appears only as the source Haehlen quoted. Metromedia overruled Varney on police-power regulation for aesthetics, a different point.

Messersmith cites the 1903 Harris v. Stearns opinion as authority that a clear tax receipt is conclusive of prior taxes paid; that opinion's affirmance was overruled and reversed on rehearing in 1906 (negated as a whole). No history noted; different litigation.

citing_name: State ex rel. Barnett v. Gray
cited_name: State ex rel. Montgomery v. Anderson
explanation: Florida court cites Montgomery v. Anderson, with parenthetical, as authority upholding a 30 percent vote requirement against equal-protection attack; North Dakota had overruled it on that validity point by 1918 (own knowledge; no excerpt). No acknowledgment.

citing_name: Miller v. International Diving & Consulting Services, Inc.
cited_name: Holmes v. J. Ray McDermott & Co.
explanation: Louisiana court cites Holmes for the conduct standard warranting punitive damages for unpaid maintenance and cure and applies it; Guevara (en banc 1995) overruled Holmes on availability of such punitive damages. Guevara not mentioned.

citing_name: International Ass'n of Machinists v. Sandsberry
explanation: Texas court string-cites Grovey to hold no governmental action in the union-shop statute; Smith v. Allwright (1944) overruled Grovey on exactly its state-action holding (own knowledge; no excerpt). No negative history noted; unrelated litigation.

Minnesota court cites McGinnis as authority sustaining employer criminal liability for a bartender's unauthorized sale; McCance (1892) overruled McGinnis on that point (own recollection; no excerpt). No acknowledgment; different litigation.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cited_name: Public Citizen Health Research Group v. Department of Health, Educatio
explanation: D.C. Circuit reversed the PSRO-is-an-agency holding (own knowledge), but Byers cites the district decision only as a contrast in a footnote, distinguishing the corporate defendants from the PSRO; it is not relied on for the holding.

cited_name: Stark County Agricultural Society v. Brenner
explanation: Logsdon relies on Brenner for the definition of joint tort liability (concert, same character of care); Meyer overruled only syllabus paragraph three, a different point (verdict against one joint defendant, per my recollection), so the negation is off point.

citing_name: O'hara v. Board of Education of the Vocational School in the County of
citing_court: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey
explanation: O'Hara cites the district decision in Moore v. Bonner as authority that the administrative hearing satisfied collateral-estoppel prerequisites; the Fourth Circuit had reversed it outright in 1982 on administrative preclusion. No subsequent history noted; unrelated litigation.

citing_court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
explanation: Benson cites the civil appeals Wilson decision for dishonesty usually being a jury question; Texas Supreme Court reversed it in 1970 as to the principal defendants, on the dishonesty determination (own recollection; no excerpt). No history noted; different litigation.

Craig cites Grasser as supporting authority that a common-law claim lies for serving a known alcoholic; Jackson v. PKM (1988) overruled that holding, finding the dram shop act exclusive (own knowledge). No acknowledgment; different litigation.

citing_name: In re Fedex Ground Package System, Inc., Employment Practices Litigati
citing_court: United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana
cited_name: Wilkinson v. Palmetto State Transp. Co.
explanation: MDL court quotes Wilkinson (S.C. App. 2006) as authority for South Carolina's right-to-control test and four factors; that decision was reversed outright by the S.C. Supreme Court in 2009; no subsequent history noted; unrelated litigation.

Court dismisses appeal taken before written judgment, citing Benton v. Smith, nine days after Gillen v. Bostick overruled Benton on premature appeals (own knowledge of Gillen; no excerpt); Gillen not mentioned though a written order had since been entered.

The reversed decision (33 Va. App. 506, miscited as Herbert) appears only in Judge Benton's dissent as a see-also on jury-waiver; the en banc majority does not use it, so the citing court did not rely on it.

citing_name: Compton v. Paul K. Harding Realty Co.
explanation: Court cites appellate Maimon v. Telman with Galler for holding that lack of a termination date does not void a shareholder agreement; that judgment was reversed outright by the Illinois Supreme Court in 1968; no history noted; different litigation.

Iowa court uses Cox's holding on the meaning of 'shown to the court' as persuasive authority for requiring proof, not assertion; Cox was overruled wholesale by Lincoln v. Territory in 1899 (no excerpt; whole-case overruling assumed on point); unacknowledged.

Court rests its remand on Moore (256 So.2d 782): consent alimony judgments are modifiable without proving changed circumstances; Bernhardt (La. 1973) overruled exactly that rule months earlier (own knowledge); Bernhardt not mentioned; different parties.

Circuit court cites Court of Appeals Jimenez for the point that failing to request an instruction is fatal; that decision was reversed and dismissed by the Virginia Supreme Court in 1991 on the instruction-default issue; no history noted; alternative ground does not remove reliance.
